# Australian CVD risk assessment quick reference

This fixture mirrors the structure of the NVDPA / Heart Foundation
quick reference guide. The wording is paraphrased and lightly invented
for testing only; nothing in this file should be treated as clinical
guidance.

## When to assess

Assess absolute CVD risk for adults aged 45 to 79 without established
cardiovascular disease. For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander
adults, begin at age 30. For people with diabetes, begin at age 35.
Reassessment intervals depend on the calculated risk band.

## Risk bands

The 2023 Australian guideline defines three bands using five-year
absolute CVD risk:

- High risk: >= 10%. Discuss intensive lifestyle interventions and
  pharmacotherapy.
- Intermediate risk: 5% to less than 10%. Discuss lifestyle changes;
  consider pharmacotherapy after shared decision-making.
- Low risk: less than 5%. Reinforce lifestyle measures and reassess
  every five years.

<!-- page break -->

## Reclassifiers

The calculator does not include all relevant variables. The following
reclassifiers may shift a patient up to the next band when present:

- Coronary artery calcium score above the age- and sex-matched 75th
  percentile.
- Family history of premature CVD (first-degree relative aged less
  than 60 years at event).
- Severe mental illness or chronic inflammatory disease.
- Ethnicity from a high-CVD-risk background, including South Asian
  and Maori or Pacific Islander populations.

## Communication

Present absolute risk as a percentage and as an icon array of 100
people. Anchor the discussion to what the patient can change. Avoid
relative-risk framing as the only number; relative risks of small
absolute numbers can mislead the conversation.
